texts.facts_text: The Applicant, apprehending arrest, in connection with the investigation of Crime No.15 of 2022 registered with Vairag Police Station, under Section 188,272, 273 and 328 of the Indian Penal Code and 26(2)(i), 26(2)(iv), 27(3)(e) and 59 of the Food and Safety and Standards Act, 2006 is seeking anticipatory bail. The aforesaid crime is registered on the basis of a complaint lodged by Ms.Pradnya Surase, Additional Commissioner of Food and Drugs Department, Solapur. The allegations is that in a raid conducted in the agricultural field of the Applicant Panmasala/Guthka which is banned has been recovered.
texts.arguments_petitioner: The learned counsel for the Applicant states that Section 328 of the IPC is only non-bailable Section and all other Sections are bailable. It is submitted that the issue of the applicability of section 328 of Indian Penal Code in such cases is pending before the Supreme Court in a batch of petitions, in which interim protection has been granted by the Supreme Court.
texts.arguments_respondent: The learned Additional Public Prosecutor seeks time.
texts.decision_text: ORDER (i) In the event of his arrest in connection with investigation of Crime No.15 of 2022 registered with Vairag Police Station, the applicant shall be released on bail on executing a P.R. Bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- with one or two solvent sureties in the like amount. (ii) The applicant shall report to the Investigating Officer on 28 February 2022 and 1 March 2022 between 11.00 am to 1.00 p.m. and as and when called by the investigating officer and shall co-operate with the Investigating Agency. (iii) In the event of breach of any of the conditions the interim protection is liable to be vacated. (iv) This order shall remain enforce till the next date. (v) Stand over to 14 March 2022.

key_facts_bullets: The Applicant is seeking anticipatory bail in connection with the investigation of Crime No.15 of 2022 registered with Vairag Police Station.
The crime involves allegations of possession of banned Panmasala/Guthka.
The complaint was lodged by Ms.Pradnya Surase, Additional Commissioner of Food and Drugs Department, Solapur.
issues_bullets: Whether the Applicant should be granted anticipatory bail.
The applicability of Section 328 of the Indian Penal Code in this case.

ml.input_text: The Applicant, apprehending arrest, in connection with the investigation of Crime No.15 of 2022 registered with Vairag Police Station, under Section 188,272, 273 and 328 of the Indian Penal Code and 26(2)(i), 26(2)(iv), 27(3)(e) and 59 of the Food and Safety and Standards Act, 2006 is seeking anticipatory bail. The aforesaid crime is registered on the basis of a complaint lodged by Ms.Pradnya Surase, Additional Commissioner of Food and Drugs Department, Solapur. The allegations is that in a raid conducted in the agricultural field of the Applicant Panmasala/Guthka which is banned has been recovered. The learned counsel for the Applicant states that Section 328 of the IPC is only non-bailable Section and all other Sections are bailable. It is submitted that the issue of the applicability of section 328 of Indian Penal Code in such cases is pending before the Supreme Court in a batch of petitions, in which interim protection has been granted by the Supreme Court. The learned Additional Public Prosecutor seeks time.
